source_refs.note: Topic 24.3.3 with the box on antibiotic resistance (PDF 221).

blocks.text: Molecular biology has recently given a wealth of information about evolutionary relationships. Just as animals have homologous structures, they also have homologous biochemicals, because structure and function rest on the genetic blueprint, DNA, found in all living things.

Related animals have similar DNA inherited from a common ancestor, and because DNA codes for proteins they also have similar proteins. Scientists extract and analyse the DNA and proteins of different organisms; by counting differences between related molecules and assuming fairly constant mutation rates, they estimate how long ago two organisms shared a common ancestral molecule.

blocks.title: How have microorganisms evolved resistance to antibiotics?
blocks.text: Antibiotic resistance means bacteria can survive exposure to an antibiotic. It may arise from mutations in bacterial genes; a resistance gene, favoured by natural selection when the antibiotic is used, is passed on to later generations of bacteria.
